title: The High Wreck
premise: Desert ranger Ansel Okafor is ordered to escort a resupply convoy upriver to the Meridian Expedition, which has gone silent in the flooded canyons of the High Wreck, a drowned pre-collapse city. He finds the survivors guarding an impossible discovery: proof that the inheritance laws propping up the ruling families are built on forged land grants, and among them, the thief he has chased for three years — his former partner Ilsa Vey. As the monsoon closes in and the families send killers to bury the truth with the expedition, Ansel must choose between the loyalty that made him a ranger and the truth that could free a nation. In the end, Ansel gets most of the expedition home alive, lets Ilsa escape with the evidence, and files a report that says nothing — while the documents surface anyway, timed to break before the rains.
about_author: Dominic Montrose is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. His novels are known for blistering chase sequences set against landscapes described with surveyor's precision.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ansel Okafor tracks a thief across the salt flats, measuring his life in distance covered rather than time lived. When orders arrive recalling him to escort an upriver convoy, he recognizes the thief's trail signature: Ilsa Vey, the partner who vanished three years ago. POV Ansel. Beat: restless duty masking old grief.

chapters.title: The Convoy Contract
chapters.summary: At Fort Calloway, Ansel meets the expedition's patron, Lady Serevan, whose family charter depends on the Meridian's success. She offers him double pay for silence as much as protection. He accepts, uneasy. POV Ansel. Beat: the first hint that this mission is about secrets, not rescue.

chapters.title: Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: The convoy pushes upriver through narrowing canyons while radio calls to the Meridian camp go unanswered. A wrecked supply raft surfaces, clawed open from inside. The young radio operator, Tam, insists someone answered once — a woman's voice saying only 'turn back.' POV Tam. Beat: dread replacing routine.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel finds boot prints matching Ilsa's gait on a gravel bar and follows them alone at night, torn between arrest and reunion. He loses her in the reeds but finds a ranger's emergency flare — hers, unspent, left deliberately. POV Ansel. Beat: hope sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Drowned City
chapters.summary: The convoy reaches the High Wreck at dawn: towers rising from floodwater, the Meridian camp strung between them like a wound. Survivors emerge armed and gaunt, led by expedition chief Dr. Amara Sen. They demand the convoy surrender its weapons. POV Dr. Sen. Beat: relief curdling into standoff.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Sen explains: three weeks ago they found the Archive Vault, and since then two expedition members have died 'accidentally.' She suspects a saboteur among her own people and won't let newcomers leave until she knows. Ansel recognizes the dead man's wounds — ranger-issue blade work. POV Ansel. Beat: trapped allies, hidden enemy.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vey steps out of the vault detail's shadows, alive and unrepentant. Privately she tells Ansel what's in the vault: land grants proving the great family charters were forged after the collapse. She didn't steal treasure; she stole proof. POV Ilsa. Beat: betrayal reframed as conviction, love rekindled against will.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Trail
chapters.summary: Ansel investigates the deaths with ranger method, finding the killer used military river-craft skills no academic possesses. Suspicion falls on expedition security chief Doran Hale, whose credentials don't check out. Hale denies everything, convincingly. POV Ansel. Beat: the hunt turns inward, trust fracturing.

chapters.title: Lady Serevan's Interest
chapters.summary: A supply skiff arrives bearing Serevan's personal envoy, who asks pointed questions about 'recovered documents' and offers extraction for select personnel. Sen refuses; the envoy's guards stay. Ansel realizes the families knew what was down here before the expedition did. POV Dr. Sen. Beat: the conspiracy has teeth and patience.

chapters.title: Vault of Forgeries
chapters.summary: Ilsa shows Ansel the vault: sealed records, a pre-collapse surveyor's confession, and charters copied in modern ink. Holding the evidence, Ansel feels his oath crack — every border he patrols rests on a lie. POV Ilsa. Beat: loyalty vs. truth becomes personal, not abstract.

chapters.title: Hale Moves
chapters.summary: Doran Hale sabotages the convoy's radios and torches the fuel cache, stranding everyone until the monsoon or a rescue that may never come. In the chaos, the envoy's guards seize the vault copies. Hale is their man after all — but not Serevan's. Someone else's. POV Tam. Beat: catastrophe, the net closing.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Storm clouds build over the canyon rim. With comms down, Ansel organizes defenses and rations; Sen catalogs who can be saved. Ilsa and Ansel keep watch together and finally speak plainly about the night she ran — she fled because he'd have had to arrest her. POV Ansel. Beat: intimacy forged under siege, love admitting itself.

chapters.title: Turn Back
chapters.summary: Tam decodes the earlier transmission: the 'woman's voice' was a warning sent by the envoy's own technician, who now begs to defect. She reveals the families' kill team is already on the river, ten days out. The defection buys them a working radio — one channel, one chance. POV Tam. Beat: fragile advantage seized from despair.

chapters.title: Divided Camp
chapters.summary: Sen wants to broadcast the forgery evidence immediately; Ilsa argues a premature signal dies with them. The camp splits into factions, and Hale's remaining sympathizers attempt to steal the originals by raft. Ansel stops them midriver in a brutal close-quarters fight. POV Dr. Sen. Beat: ideals colliding when unity matters most.

chapters.title: The Kill Team Arrives
chapters.summary: Two gunboats enter the canyon flying no colors. In the first exchange, the defector technician is killed and the convoy's lead driver wounded. Ansel reads the attackers' discipline: these are family retainers, professionals. Retreat upstream is cut off. POV Ansel. Beat: the enemy becomes real, lethal, patient.

chapters.title: Serevan's Bargain
chapters.summary: The envoy offers terms: hand over Ilsa and the originals, and everyone else walks free before the monsoon. Sen prepares to accept. Ansel, asked to make the arrest he's owed for three years, instead tells Sen the truth about the charters — burning his own oath in front of witnesses. POV Ansel. Beat: the central choice made, loyalty to people over institution.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: The storm hits: the canyon floods twenty feet in hours, drowning the lower camp and scattering the gunboats' moorings. In the chaos, Ansel and Ilsa run the rapids on a jury-rigged raft carrying the originals, pursued by one surviving gunboat. POV Ilsa. Beat: nature as equal-opportunity executioner, desperate flight.

chapters.title: The Wreck Run
chapters.summary: The chase threads the drowned towers — Ilsa navigating by memory of her survey days, Ansel shooting out the gunboat's spotlight. They ground the pursuer on a submerged spire but capsize themselves, losing half the documents to the river. POV Ansel. Beat: triumph and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: What Survives the Water
chapters.summary: Washed ashore downstream, they find the core evidence intact — the surveyor's signed confession, waterproofed in tin. But Ilsa is feverish from the immersion, and the monsoon has weeks left to fall. Ansel carries her toward the relay station at Calloway Gap. POV Ilsa. Beat: tenderness and urgency entwined.

chapters.title: Calloway Gap
chapters.summary: At the relay station, Ansel faces the final choice: transmit the evidence himself and end his career, or let Ilsa vanish with it and preserve his report's clean lie. He does both — sends her downriver with the tin, then broadcasts an anonymous data burst he knows the families will trace too late. POV Ansel. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Ansel returns to Fort Calloway with eleven survivors and files his official account: equipment failure, storm losses, nothing recovered. Lady Serevan reads it and understands exactly what he isn't saying; neither presses. Sen chooses exile over silence, taking the story to the coastal papers. POV Dr. Sen. Beat: quiet complicity, truth outsourced to the brave.

chapters.title: First Rain on Clean Ground
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the forged charters break nationwide; the Serevan charter is suspended pending inquiry. Ansel, stripped of rank but not imprisoned, walks the salt flats again — and finds fresh boot prints with Ilsa's gait heading north, an unspent flare beside them. He smiles and follows. POV Ansel. Beat: love against duty resolved into a new road.
